claims.text: The as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons contain residual stresses from deposition.
The as-deposited material contains deposition-induced heterogeneities.
A rapid, low-temperature anneal will partially relax residual stresses in the nanoscale material.
The proposed anneal can relax residual stress without significant grain coarsening.
Rapid low-temperature annealing will reduce residual-strain gradients.
Rapid low-temperature annealing will lower the density of interfacial defects such as grain boundaries and dislocations.
Grain boundaries and dislocations act as pinning centers for magnetic-domain motion in this alloy system.
A magnetostructural phase transition governs the magnetocaloric effect in the nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi material.
Stress relief will allow the magnetostructural transition to proceed more uniformly.
Reduced defect-mediated domain pinning will decrease hysteresis losses during magnetic-cooling cycles.
More homogeneous and reversible magnetostructural transformation will enhance the net magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
Annealed samples will have a smaller magnetic-hysteresis width than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a larger temperature change per unit magnetic-field change than the as-deposited baseline.
The unannealed baseline has more pronounced hysteresis because of residual stress and defect-induced pinning.
The unannealed baseline has a less optimal magnetocaloric response because of residual stress and defect-induced pinning.
The magnetic-cooling cycle frequency is limited by the intrinsic heat-transfer rate of the sample.
The proposed test compares annealed and unannealed samples under identical magnetic-field cycling and thermal conditions.

Failure of annealing to produce both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and a corresponding magnetocaloric enhancement relative to the control would falsify the proposed strain-relief mechanism.
